headline: State Park Trail Permits and Gorge Reservations
reservation: Flume Gorge requires date-specific advanced reservations through the official New Hampshire State Parks portal. While the park is open year-round, specific attractions and parking lots may implement reservation-only systems during peak autumn foliage weeks; always verify current requirements before arrival.

days.title: Granite Gorges and Glacial Basins

stops.name: Flume Gorge
stops.detail: Walk the two-mile loop featuring boardwalks along towering granite walls and cascading waterfalls.

stops.name: The Basin
stops.detail: Observe the 20-foot wide granite pothole formed by glacial meltwater at the base of a waterfall.

days.driving: Allow 20–40 minutes for travel within the Notch; conditions vary
days.note: Boardwalks can be slippery when wet; sturdy walking shoes are recommended for the Flume Gorge loop.

days.title: Alpine Vistas and Historic Valleys

stops.name: Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway
stops.detail: Ascend to the summit for views of the Presidential Range and Vermont's Green Mountains.

stops.name: Profile Lake
stops.detail: Visit the Old Man of the Mountain Profiler Plaza to learn the history of the fallen stone icon.

days.driving: Allow 15–30 minutes for transfers; conditions vary
days.note: Summit weather is significantly colder than the valley; check the mountain forecast before ascending.

days.title: Lakeside Reflection and Shoreline Paths

stops.name: Echo Lake Beach
stops.detail: Relax by the water or rent a boat to view the Franconia Range from the lake surface.

stops.name: Artists Bluff Trail
stops.detail: A short but rocky ascent providing a classic view of the notch and Echo Lake below.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local park access; conditions vary
days.note: Parking at Echo Lake fills very early on summer weekends; have a secondary plan for parking.

intel.title: Trailhead and Attraction Lots
intel.text: Major lots at Flume Gorge and Cannon Mountain are paved, but hiking trailheads like Falling Waters often fill by early morning. Shuttles may operate seasonally to alleviate congestion at popular trailheads.

intel.title: Mountain Valley Reception
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable along I-93 but vanishes quickly on higher elevation trails and in deep wooded sections. Download offline maps for any hiking activities.

intel.title: Valley Service Hubs
intel.text: Lincoln and North Woodstock to the south and Franconia to the north are the last reliable spots for fuel and supplies. There are no gas stations within the park boundaries along the Notch Parkway.

intel.title: Seasonal Operations
intel.text: The Tramway and Flume Gorge are typically seasonal, operating from late May through mid-October. High-elevation snow can persist on trails through June.

intel.title: Pavement and Paths
intel.text: The Franconia Notch Bike Path is a paved multi-use trail connecting many sights, providing an alternative to driving. Some hiking trails require crossing the Pemigewasset River via footbridges.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental vehicle at Lebanon Municipal Airport (LEB) and drive north for approximately 75 minutes to reach the gateway towns of Lincoln or Woodstock.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved Notch Parkway; check winter rental restrictions if visiting during the snowy shoulder seasons.
plan.goldenHour: Artists Bluff is a renowned viewpoint for sunset over the notch, though rocks can be treacherous in fading light; bring a headlamp.
